recent_articles.title: Shivakumar’s elevation as Karnataka CM poses existential challenge for JD(S) - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **H.D. Kumaraswamy** and **D.K. Shivakumar**, both members of the Vokkaliga community, are facing a potential political challenge as the change in leadership within Karnataka's Congress-led government raises concerns for the **Janata Dal (Secular)**. The party is considering possible decisions that could see **Kumaraswamy** return to full-time State politics, which some view as disadvantageous given his rivalry with **Shivakumar**.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka government formation LIVE: Congress to convene crucial CLP meeting at 4 p.m. on May 30 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, after resigning as the chief minister of Karnataka, met with **Rahul Gandhi** at **Sonia Gandhi’s** residence. The meeting focused on his future role within the **Congress** party and included discussions about his son's potential positions in the new government.  **Siddaramaiah** also met with **Mallikarjun Kharge**, the Congress chief, to discuss the transition process.

recent_articles.title: Before relinquishing office, Siddaramaiah demolishes long-held myth linking Chamarajanagar visits to a Chief Minister’s fall from power - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, Karnataka's longest-serving Chief Minister, visited Chamarajanagar town despite a long-held superstition that visiting the district would lead to power loss.  He consistently defied the belief, having visited the region multiple times during his two terms as Chief Minister and even convening a Cabinet meeting there last year. **Siddaramaiah** dismissed the superstition, stating he had no faith in it and that his political position had strengthened after each visit.

recent_articles.title: Siddaramaiah and D.K. Shivakumar: A public bonhomie that never let up - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Despite internal tensions within the **Congress** in Karnataka, **Siddaramaiah** and **Shivakumar**, leaders of opposing factions, maintained a cordial public image.  They were seen discussing power transfer in Delhi and even embraced after **Siddaramaiah's** resignation. Their unity was evident throughout their tenure, with frequent appearances together and gestures of support for each other. The transition of power from **Siddaramaiah** to **Shivakumar**, though initially feared to be messy, unfolded smoothly.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka politics LIVE: Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah announces decision to step down at breakfast meeting with Ministers - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, Karnataka's Chief Minister, announced his resignation during a breakfast meeting at his residence on May 28th. He informed his Cabinet colleagues that he had been asked to step down by the **Congress High Command**.  He will visit the Governor’s office and address a press conference later in the day. The Congress Legislative Party is expected to meet on Friday (May 29, 2026) to discuss the likely successor.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah announces decision to step down at breakfast meeting with Ministers - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, the Chief Minister of Karnataka, announced his resignation from the post during a breakfast meeting at his residence on May 28th. He informed his Cabinet colleagues that he had been asked to step down by the **Congress High Command**.  The decision comes after speculation about his continuation and an offer of a Rajya Sabha seat from **Rahul Gandhi**, Leader of Opposition in Rajya Sabha, who requested him to pave the way for a new leader. The Governor, **Thaawarchand Gehlot**, is expected to meet with **Siddaramaiah** before accepting his resignation.

recent_articles.title: Will Siddaramaiah's breakfast with Cabinet colleagues on May 28 end with leadership change in Karnataka? - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, the Chief Minister of Karnataka, has invited his Cabinet colleagues for a breakfast meeting on Thursday to address speculation about his future.  The Congress high command has asked him to move to the Rajya Sabha, paving the way for a leadership change. **Randeep Singh Surjewala**, the All India Congress Committee general secretary in charge of Karnataka, arrived in Bengaluru to facilitate the transition process. While some party members are pushing for his resignation, he has refused to comment on the matter and only stated that he will speak tomorrow.

recent_articles.title: Leadership tussle in Karnataka: Congress high command wants Siddaramaiah to move to Rajya Sabha, sources say, even as party officially denies - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, the current Chief Minister of **Karnataka**, is facing pressure to step down after a meeting with the **Congress** high command in New Delhi. The discussions centered on selecting candidates for Rajya Sabha and Legislative Council elections, but sources suggest that leadership change was also a key topic.  Despite official denials, there are indications that the party may be considering a shift in leadership if **Siddaramaiah** doesn't agree to step down.  The high command is facing pressure to make a decision before June 8th deadline for Rajya Sabha nominations.

recent_articles.title: Leader of Opposition R. Ashok criticises Congress government - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **R. Ashok**, the **Opposition Leader in the Legislative Assembly**, criticized the **Congress party's** internal power struggle, stating that it has rendered the Karnataka government dysfunctional. He claimed that most ministers are in Delhi while the state administration lacks direction, and the high command is ineffective in restoring order.  **Siddaramaiah**, the Chief Minister of Karnataka, faces accusations of accumulating excessive debt through "unscientific and fiscally irresponsible guarantee schemes," according to **Ashok**.

recent_articles.title: Leadership change in Karnataka? CM Siddaramaiah to fly to Delhi amid speculation - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Hindu** has updated its commenting platform. Users must now comment in full sentences using English and abide by community guidelines.  Comments will be moderated to ensure they are respectful and constructive.

recent_articles.title: Bengaluru: Toyota BizIntel Hub to come up at KWIN City with ₹1,200 cr. investment - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Toyota Kirloskar Motor (TKM)** signed an agreement with the **Karnataka government** to establish its global-standard BizIntel Hub at KWIN City in Bengaluru. The project, valued at ₹1,200 crore, will create approximately 200 jobs and encompass vehicle manufacturing, testing activities, and an advanced automobile manufacturing facility.  The first phase of the project involves 300 acres of land allotted to **TKM**, with a projected investment of ₹48,000 crore across five phases. The initiative aims to foster innovation, healthcare, and information technology in KWIN City.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka’s hijab row: A rollback, at last - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Karnataka's** Minister for School Education and Literacy Madhu Bangarappa announced the rollback of a 2022 order banning hijab in schools and pre-university colleges. The controversial order, implemented by the previous **BJP** government, sparked protests across the state after six Muslim girls were barred from entering their classrooms in Udupi.  The move was a manifesto promise of the Congress party but had been delayed for nearly three years.

recent_articles.title: Disambiguating a year of flux: expert panels at The Hindu Huddle, 2026 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The sixth edition of The Hindu Group's ideas conclave, The Hindu Huddle, will be held in Bengaluru on June 5 and 6, 2026.  **Siddaramaiah**, **D.K. Shivakumar**, and other Chief Ministers from across the country will participate alongside Union Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship **Jayant Chaudhary**, **Omar Abdullah**, **A. Revanth Reddy**, and **K.G. Arunraj**. The event will feature discussions on topics such as tariffs' impact on the Indian economy, diplomacy in managing crises, and artificial intelligence's influence on various aspects of life.  **The Hindu Huddle** is presented by the Sami-Sabinsa Group and co-powered by the Government of Telangana.

recent_articles.title: Congress asks its rank and file to be alert against deletion of voters ahead of SIR exercise in Karnataka - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** leaders are concerned about the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise in Karnataka, fearing voter suppression similar to what happened in West Bengal. The party has urged its rank and file to remain vigilant and is preparing for potential challenges. **Randeep Surjewala**, Congress general secretary in charge of Karnataka, emphasized the importance of educating voters about SIR's implications.  The State government is expected to respond to the concerns raised by the party soon.

recent_articles.title: Nine dead in Bhatkal estuary, two missing - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nine people**, including eight from an extended family, died in a tragic incident near Shirali in Uttara Kannada, **India**. The victims were reportedly collecting shellfish when they were swept away by strong currents caused by recent rainfall.  The deceased have been identified as Malati Jattappa Naik, Laxmi Mahadev Naik, and others.  **Police**, **SDRF**, and **Fire and Emergency Services** are searching for two missing individuals while the **Chief Minister of Karnataka**, **Siddaramaiah**, expressed condolences to the families of the victims.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka to soon get India’s second largest international cricket stadium - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, the Chief Minister of **Karnataka**, announced the construction of a new international cricket stadium in Suryanagar, Anekal Taluk. The 80,000-seat stadium will be the second largest in India and is expected to boost sports development, tourism, and economic growth in the area.  The project has faced opposition from some farmers and environmentalists who raised concerns about the impact on wildlife and land value. **Siddaramaiah** assured that farmers would receive fair compensation and land allocation for their surrendered properties. The CM also launched the 'Namma Mane' housing programme, which will provide affordable housing to residents of Suryanagar.

recent_articles.title: States should be allowed to conduct CET for medical courses: CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** called for the decentralization of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) and urged **States** to have the opportunity to conduct their own Common Entrance Tests (CET) for medical courses. He argued that education is a concurrent list subject, allowing states to independently administer entrance exams for professional courses within the federal system.

recent_articles.title: Bidadi township: Deve Gowda announces stir against project; DKS hits back - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **H.D. Deve Gowda**, former Prime Minister, launched a campaign against the proposed Bidadi township project, claiming it targets fertile agricultural land and is driven by a "land business." He accused the **Siddaramaiah** government of facilitating this project under the guise of urban development, drawing parallels with previous satellite township projects that were withdrawn due to public opposition. **D.K. Shivakumar**, Deputy Chief Minister, countered Gowda's accusations, alleging that the Kumaraswamy family amassed wealth through real estate dealings and initiated similar projects in the past.

recent_articles.title: ST delegation meets CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, the Chief Minister of Karnataka, has promised to convene an all-party meeting to discuss the inclusion of a 56% reservation matrix in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution.  He also assured **V.S. Ugrappa**, former MP and leader of the Samana Manaskara Vedike, that he will take an all-party delegation to **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** to advocate for this legislation. The state government has been working to overturn a legal stay on the 56% reservation, with legal experts being consulted and a special leave petition potentially filed in the Supreme Court.

recent_articles.title: Siddaramaiah launches counter-attack, accuses Modi of destroying dignity of Prime Minister’s post - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, the Chief Minister of Karnataka, criticized **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** for his recent speech in Bengaluru, accusing him of using "lies, poor taste, hatred and jealousy" to undermine the Prime Minister's office.  **Siddaramaiah** questioned the authenticity of the speech, suggesting it reflected poorly on **Modi**'s government and party in Karnataka.

recent_articles.title: CM is unsettled by PM’s remarks: BJP - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **BJP** in Karnataka responded to **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah's** criticism of **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, stating that the Prime Minister's speech at a BJP event was within his democratic right. The opposition leader, R. Ashok, argued that the Prime Minister spoke about issues affecting 7 crore Kannadigas and that Siddaramaiah should focus on addressing real concerns in Karnataka rather than being rattled by the remarks.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka minister D Sudhakar passes away - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D. Sudhakar**, the Minister for Planning and Statistics of **Karnataka**, passed away on Sunday at a private hospital in Bengaluru after battling a lung infection following a knee operation. He was 66 years old.  The government has declared a three-day mourning period and a holiday for schools, colleges, and government establishments on Monday. Prominent leaders across party lines have expressed condolences, including **Randeep Singh Surjewala**, the AICC general secretary in charge of Karnataka, and **Siddaramaiah**, the Chief Minister of **Karnataka**.

recent_articles.title: Gram panchayat elections in Karnataka will be held before end of 2026, says Minister Priyank Kharge - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Priyank Kharge**, **Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister**, announced that the state government will hold gram panchayat elections before the end of the year.  He also stated that drinking water scarcity in Kalaburagi district is being addressed with funds from the state government, the Kalyana Karnataka Region Development Board, and recommendations from task forces headed by MLAs. **Mr. Kharge** added that a decision on expanding the State Cabinet will be made at the appropriate time by **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** and the party high command.

recent_articles.title: SC order on Mysuru heritage structures: MP seeks immediate restoration works - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar**, **Mysuru MP**, urged **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** to release funds and begin restoration work on the historic Devaraja Market and Lansdowne Building following a Supreme Court ruling that ordered their conservation instead of demolition. The court's decision, based on an IIT Roorkee assessment, found nearly 70% of the structures could be repaired and restored while retaining the existing foundation. **Wadiyar** emphasized the importance of preserving Mysuru’s historic architecture and urged the State government to use allocated funds exclusively for conservation efforts.

recent_articles.title: CM to visit Mysuru on Wednesday - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** is scheduled to visit Mysuru on Wednesday. He will participate in Shivayogi Siddarameshwara Jayanti celebrations at Kalamandira, where he will confer the Kayakayogi Sri Shivayogi Siddarameshwara award.  He will also attend a private program later that evening before departing for Bengaluru on May 7th.

recent_articles.title: Results of bypolls to two Assembly seats in Karnataka on May 4 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Congress** government is hoping to retain both Davangere South and Bagalkot constituencies in upcoming bypolls, despite the BJP's confidence in winning both.  **Samarth Mallikarjun**, a Congress candidate in Davangere South, faces off against **T. Srinivas Dasakariappa**, while **Umesh Meti**, son of senior Congress leader H.Y. Meti, is contesting against **Veeranna Charanthimath** in Bagalkot.  The Congress is closely watching the Dalit Left communities' voting patterns and the impact of the SDPI on its Muslim voter base. The party will be evaluating the results in light of recent setbacks for the Congress, including the expulsion of MLCs Abdul Jabbar and Nazeer Ahmed.

recent_articles.title: Rayaraddi urges for Mallikarjun Kharge as Karnataka Chief Minister if Siddaramaiah is to be replaced - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Basavaraj Rayaraddi**, Chief Minister Siddaramaiah's economic adviser, stated that there is no need to change the Chief Minister and suggested **Mallikarjun Kharge**, AICC president, as a potential alternative if the party decides on a leadership change.  Rayaraddi met with **Kharge** last week and urged him to resolve the ongoing confusion surrounding the leadership in Karnataka.

recent_articles.title: Preparations in full swing in Bagalkot for counting of bypoll votes today - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Officials** are preparing for the counting of votes in the Bagalkot Assembly bypoll, scheduled to begin at 8 a.m. on Monday. The counting will take place at the University of Horticultural Sciences with **23 rounds** of counting and arrangements for postal ballots and voters over 80 years old.  The election is considered a contest between **Umesh Meti**, son of the late MLA H.Y. Meti, and **Veeranna (Veerabhadrayya) Charantimath** of the BJP. The main contenders are expected to benefit from the sympathy factor surrounding the death of H.Y. Meti and the political campaigning by **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah**, **Public Works Minister Satish Jarkiholi**, and **BJP State president B.Y. Vijayendra**.

recent_articles.title: Constant churn in Karnataka CMO in this tenure of Siddaramaiah raises eyebrows - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **S. Ravi**, the head of **State Intelligence** in Karnataka, was unexpectedly replaced by **Labhu Ram** on April 28th. This is the fourth change in leadership for the position under the current **Siddaramaiah** government, which has seen three previous chiefs removed without clear explanations.

recent_articles.title: Bowring tragedy: CM orders suspension of official, Lokayukta takes up inquiry, police file only UDR - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following the tragic collapse of a compound wall at **Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital**, which killed seven people, **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** ordered the suspension of the executive engineer involved and directed a notice to be issued to the hospital authorities. The **Lokayukta** has registered a suo motu case and initiated an inquiry into the incident.  The **Bengaluru City Police** filed an Unnatural Death Report (UDR) but have not yet registered an FIR against any authorities for alleged negligence. An investigation is underway to determine the cause of the collapse, with experts from the Public Works Department and the India Meteorological Department consulted.

recent_articles.title: Bengaluru weather highlights: Orange alert issued for Bengaluru, south Karnataka districts; traffic police release advisory for commuters - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **CM Siddaramaiah** visited injured individuals after a portion of the Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital compound wall collapsed in Shivajinagar, killing seven people.  The **Medical Education Minister Sharanprakash R. Patil** ordered safety audits for government hospital buildings. The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** issued an orange alert for Bengaluru, urging caution from motorists due to heavy rainfall.

recent_articles.title: Residents urge BMRCL to include ‘Bilekahalli’ in IIMB metro station name on Bengaluru’s Pink Line metro - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Residents** in south Bengaluru have written to **Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL)**, urging them to rename the upcoming “IIMB” metro station on the Pink Line as “IIMB–Bilekahalli” to recognize the locality’s identity.  The residents argue that naming the station solely after an institution risks overlooking the cultural context of the area and propose a name that balances modern infrastructure with local heritage. While **BMRCL** has received the letter, they confirmed that renaming a metro station involves a detailed procedure and requires approval from both state and central governments. This issue reflects a larger trend in Bengaluru where renaming metro stations is becoming increasingly contentious.

recent_articles.title: ED raids a political vendetta, claims Nalapad; Congress leaders question timing - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Enforcement Directorate (ED)** conducted searches at various locations in Bengaluru on Tuesday as part of a cybercrime and cryptocurrency-related money laundering case involving **Srikrishna Ramesh**, also known as Sriki.  **Mohammed Haris Nalapad**, son of Congress MLA N.A. Haris, claimed the action was politically motivated, alleging it aimed to derail his father's ministerial prospects. **The ED has not yet issued a statement regarding the outcome or evidence collected.**  **Congress leaders** have accused the **BJP** of targeting them through investigating agencies, citing similar raids not being conducted on **BJP leaders**. **Siddaramaiah**, the Chief Minister, and other officials expressed concern over the timing of the raids and questioned their relevance.

recent_articles.title: Special Cabinet meeting in Karnataka to discuss internal reservation on April 24 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Karnataka** government will hold a special Cabinet meeting this Friday to discuss the internal reservation matrix for 101 Scheduled Castes within the existing 15% reservation. The decision follows pressure from Dalit groups, including Ministers K.H. Muniyappa and R.B. Thimmapur, who demanded its finalization. A technical committee is reviewing the issue of categorization, ratio for each category, and roster points, with a report expected before the meeting.

recent_articles.title: Yathindra draws line between legacy politics and JD(S) ‘family politics’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Yathindra Siddaramaiah**, a **Congress MLC**, clarified that his entry into politics was driven by a desire to uphold his father's legacy, not to engage in bribery as alleged by **H.D. Kumaraswamy**.  He stated that he became involved in politics after the death of his elder brother and emphasized the need to continue his father's political work and protect his supporters.

recent_articles.title: Davanagere bypoll: Karnataka CM’s political secretary Naseer Ahmed sacked - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following allegations of anti-party activities during the Davanagere South Assembly bypoll, **Naseer Ahmed**, MLC and former Political Secretary to Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, has been removed from his post.  **Abdul Jabbar**, KPCC Minority Cell chairperson, resigned in response to the accusations, which included lobbying for a Muslim candidate and opposing the Congress nominee. The **Department of Personnel and Administrative Reforms** issued an order relieving **Ahmed** of his responsibilities after he declined to step down voluntarily.

recent_articles.title: Davangere South bypolls: Tanveer Sait too alleges embarrassment to Congress by some minority leaders - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tanveer Sait**, former Minister and **KPCC** working president, criticized the party's handling of the recent Davangere South by-election, claiming confusion among voters was caused by internal conflicts. He stated that while minority leaders seeking a ticket for their community members is not wrong, they should follow party decisions.  Sait also defended the decision to field Samarth, grandson of **Shamanur Shivashankarappa**, citing the "sympathy" factor in ticket distribution and acknowledged past instances where he benefited from this practice. He further claimed that despite instructions from **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** and **KPCC president D.K. Shivakumar** to address rebel leaders' concerns, they failed to act.  Local leaders have called for action against those responsible for voter confusion.

recent_articles.title: Education powerful tool to break out of all shackles, says Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** emphasized the importance of education in achieving an egalitarian society during Ambedkar's birth anniversary celebrations. He highlighted the role of **Ambedkar**, who he credits with creating the Constitution, and stressed that despite its provisions for freedom, equality, and brotherhood, full equality remains elusive after 76 years.  **Siddaramaiah** acknowledged the power of education in breaking down societal barriers.

recent_articles.title: Stalin warns of massive protests against delimitation; Revanth calls for united southern front - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Ministers** of non-BJP-ruled states, particularly in southern India, are opposing the **Union Government’s** proposal for delimitation ahead of women's reservation.  **Tamil Nadu** CM M.K. Stalin threatened a massive protest if the proposal affects Southern States and urged a united front against the "pro rata" formula. **Telangana** CM Revanth Reddy called for a national consensus on seat expansion, proposing a hybrid model that would allocate seats based on population and GSDP.  **Karnataka** CM Siddaramaiah warned that even with percentage increases, delimitation would disproportionately benefit large states controlled by the BJP, diminishing the influence of Southern States.

recent_articles.title: CM’s political secretary Naseer Ahmed ‘asked’ to quit - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following allegations of anti-party activities by some Muslim leaders in the Davangere South Assembly bypoll, **Abdul Jabbar**, chairman of the **KPCC Minority Cell** resigned.  His resignation followed a request from **Siddaramaiah’s** political secretary, **Naseer Ahmed**, to step down. Two Muslim leaders and Housing Minister B.Z. Zameer Ahmed Khan are accused of not campaigning for the Congress candidate, Samarth Mallikarjun, potentially impacting the election outcome.

recent_articles.title: Khandre seeks continuation of Bidar–Bengaluru flight service; hails Chief Minister’s support to region - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Eshwar B. Khandre**, **Karnataka's Forest, Ecology and Environment Minister**, urged **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** to sustain the Bidar-Bengaluru flight service, which was reinstated with state support last year after being suspended due to a withdrawal of federal subsidy under the UDAN scheme. The service, costing ₹13 crore in financial assistance from the **Kalyana Karnataka Region Development Board (KKRDB)**, resumed on April 16th, 2023.

recent_articles.title: Speculative journalism dangerous, says Siddaramaiah at State journalists’ meet - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** cautioned against "speculative journalism" during the 40th State conference of the **Karnataka Working Journalists’ Association**. He urged journalists to contribute to social reform and uphold constitutional values, emphasizing the role of media in a democracy.  He also expressed concern over superstition despite increasing education levels and highlighted the need for promoting scientific temper through education. The Chief Minister assured continued support for free bus passes for rural journalists and pledged to address any implementation issues.

recent_articles.title: Scientific temper, rational thinking key to eradicating caste, says Chief Minister Siddaramaiah - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** called for the eradication of caste discrimination through rational thought and scientific temper, emphasizing unity in a diverse society. He urged against divisive forces seeking to pit communities against each other and stressed the importance of 'kayaka' and 'dasoha' principles for an equitable society.  **Mr. Siddaramaiah** also highlighted the need to reject superstition and embrace education with a rational outlook. **Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Priyank Kharge** announced additional funding for the development of the Bhojalingeshwara Mutt.

recent_articles.title: Infighting among minority leaders: MLC Abdul Jabbar quits KPCC minority cell chief’s post - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Abdul Jabbar**, a three-time MLC, resigned as **KPCC Minority Cell chief** in response to infighting within the party over the Davangere South byelection. The resignation follows accusations of inadequate campaigning by leaders close to **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah**, including **B.Z. Zameer Ahmed Khan**, and pressure for action against him.  The unrest stems from a denial of a party ticket to a Muslim candidate, leading to discontent among minority leaders like **Saleem Ahmed** and **Rizwan Arshad**.  A detailed report recommending action against those accused of undermining the official candidate has been submitted to the high command.

recent_articles.title: Bengaluru's new cricket stadium? KHB invites bids for 80,000-seater in Anekal amid push for larger venue - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Karnataka Housing Board (KHB)** has issued tenders for the construction of a new international cricket stadium in Anekal, Bengaluru. The project, estimated at ₹943.46 crore and to be executed on an EPC Mode-1 turnkey basis, will have a seating capacity of 80,000 and is expected to become one of the largest cricket stadiums in India. Eligible contractors registered with Central Public Works Department, Karnataka Public Works Department, or other State government agencies can participate in the bidding process.  The project was announced this year in the State Budget as part of a larger sports complex called 'KHB Surya Kreeda Grama'.

recent_articles.title: Congress discusses women’s reservation law and delimitation; Kharge to meet other Opposition leaders for joint strategy - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Congress Working Committee** (CWC) discussed the government's proposed delimitation exercise and women's reservation law implementation. The party plans to formulate a joint strategy for the upcoming special session of Parliament, aiming to implement the women's reservation law by 2029 and increase the strength of the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies by 50%.  **Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge**, **Sonia Gandhi**, and **Rahul Gandhi** expressed concerns about the proposed changes, emphasizing the need for wider consultation on delimitation. The party also criticized the government's move to implement a predetermined number of seats for women, arguing that it undermines proportional representation for other marginalized groups.

recent_articles.title: Chief Minister to attend Congress Working Committee meeting on April 10 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, the Chief Minister of Karnataka, is scheduled to travel to New Delhi for a meeting with the **Congress Working Committee (CWC)** on Friday. He will discuss the political situation and the LPG crisis in the state at the meeting, as well as seek clearance for pending proposals from **Union Ministers**.  **Siddaramaiah** is expected to return to Bengaluru that evening.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka bypolls at 1 PM: 42% polling in Bagalkot; 37.17% in Davanagere South - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Voting for by-elections in Bagalkot and Davanagere South constituencies in Karnataka is underway.  **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah**, **Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar**, and several other ministers campaigned extensively in the two segments, while the BJP focused on unity among its leaders. The outcome of the by-election is unlikely to have an immediate impact on state politics but is seen as a matter of prestige for both the ruling Congress and the opposition BJP. Over 2.59 lakh eligible voters are expected to cast their ballots in Bagalkot, where nine candidates are vying for the seat, and over 2.31 lakh voters in Davanagere South, with 25 candidates contesting.  The counting of votes will be held on May 4th.

recent_articles.title: Chief Minister Siddaramaiah accuses Election Commission of India of being ‘selective and complicit’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** criticized the **Election Commission of India (ECI)** for its request for information on funds released under Karnataka's guarantee schemes in Davangere and Bagalkot districts, where byelections are scheduled.  He accused the ECI of exhibiting a "double standard" by being more active when the state fulfills its promises than when the **BJP** or **NDA** governments act.

recent_articles.title: Deve Gowda, HDK, Chalavadi joined hands with BJP for their own political existence, says Chief Minister Siddaramaiah - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** criticized former Prime Minister **H.D. Deve Gowda**, former Chief Minister **H.D. Kumaraswamy**, and Leader of the Opposition in Legislative Council **Chalavadi Narayanaswamy** for joining the BJP, claiming they are only seeking political survival.  He accused them of hypocrisy for criticizing the RSS and **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** while now aligning with the party. **Siddaramaiah** also highlighted the people's support for the state government's guarantee schemes and criticized the BJP for opposing them.

recent_articles.title: Parameshwara says he expects Siddaramaiah to continue as Chief Minister for the rest of the term - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **G. Parameshwara**, **Siddaramaiah**, and the **Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC)** have addressed recent speculation about leadership in the state.  Parameshwara stated that while the party high command did not explicitly mandate a full term for Siddaramaiah's leadership, he will continue as Chief Minister until the end of his term in 2028. He dismissed claims of confusion and emphasized that the high command has never discussed the leadership issue. Parameshwara also expressed confidence in the Congress winning upcoming bypolls and attributed this to the government's commitment to fulfilling promises and development programs.

recent_articles.title: Bagalkot bypoll campaign focussed on attacks on individual leaders, leaving out real issues - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The by-elections in **Karnataka** saw a focus on personal attacks rather than addressing key issues like drought and farm labor migration.  **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah**, **Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar**, and **Law and Parliamentary Affairs Minister H.K. Patil** criticized the BJP candidate, **Viranna Charantimath**, for his perceived arrogance and lack of accessibility to rural voters. **Basanagouda R. Patil Yatnal**, a close friend of **Charantimath**, also targeted minority groups and accused him of behaving inappropriately with people.  While both parties engaged in meetings with various caste groups, the campaign was dominated by personal attacks rather than substantive policy discussions.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka bypolls: Congress, BJP trade charges to sway voters - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** and **BJP** leaders are intensifying their campaigns for the upcoming byelections in Davanagere South and Bagalkot, with accusations of financial mismanagement and voter manipulation.  **Randeep Singh Surjewala**, AICC general secretary in charge of Karnataka, accused the **Modi government** of denying Karnataka its rightful share in taxes and funds, while **B.S. Yediyurappa** and **R. Ashok**, BJP leaders, claimed that the **Congress government** has squandered resources through corruption and inflated prices for essential services to fund its guarantees.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka bypolls: Minister Zameer Ahmed Khan begins campaign in Davangere - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **B.Z. Zameer Ahmed Khan**, the **Housing, Minority Welfare, and Waqf Minister**, arrived in Davangere to campaign for the Congress candidate, **Samarth Mallikarjun**.  He clarified that his absence from the campaign was due to prior commitments as the star campaigner in Kerala and denied any ill will towards **S.S. Mallikarjun** or his family. He assured that he would work to ensure a successful campaign for the Congress candidate, despite some internal party discussions regarding ticket distribution.  He also stated his intention to convince MLC Abdul Jabbar to join the campaign efforts.

recent_articles.title: Delimitation: Modi’s remark is more like election-driven, says Siddaramaiah - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, the Chief Minister of Karnataka, criticized **Prime Minister Modi's** statement regarding southern states' Lok Sabha seat distribution. He argued that while all states would gain seats, the scale of increase appears to favor BJP-dominated states, disproportionately benefiting them over southern states.  He claimed that this could widen regional imbalances and penalize states with successful population control and governance. **Siddaramaiah** vowed to oppose any attempt to weaken Karnataka's voice in the matter.

recent_articles.title: Davangere South: Close contest on the cards while minorities are divided over supporting Shamanur family - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, the **Chief Minister of Karnataka**, returned to Davangere on Sunday to campaign for the upcoming byelection in the constituency, facing a divided AHINDA vote.  The constituency has seen an unprecedented increase in Muslim candidates this election, with 13 out of 25 candidates being from the community. The outcome will likely hinge on the decision of minority voters, particularly Muslims, who have been demanding representation and are concerned about the lack of development in the area compared to Davangere North.  The voting patterns indicate that Muslim votes determine victory in the constituency.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka bypolls: DKS helping BJP indirectly, says R. Ashok - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **R. Ashok**, leader of the Opposition in the Assembly, accused **D.K. Shivakumar**, the Deputy Chief Minister and KPCC president, of indirectly assisting the BJP in the upcoming bypolls to two Karnataka Assembly seats.  He claimed that some senior Congress leaders are aiding the BJP's campaign, including Mr. Shivakumar, who aims to become Chief Minister if the Congress loses the bypolls. **Mr. Ashok** also alleged that NSUI students were spreading misinformation about the BJP candidate and that police inaction against them is indicative of a bias towards the Congress. He demanded a fair election and urged voters to cast their ballots without fear.

recent_articles.title: Search operations stepped up to trace missing Kerala woman trekker in Tadiandamol in Kodagu - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Forest Minister Eshwar Khandre** and **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** have ordered intensified search operations for 36-year-old G. Sharanya, who went missing during a trek to Tandiandamol in Kodagu district on April 2nd.  A total of nine teams are involved in the search, including personnel from the police, anti-Naxal force, dog squad, and forest staff.  **Ms. Sharanya**, a resident of Kozhikode, Kerala, contacted her homestay to report getting lost before disappearing. Local tribal communities have also joined the efforts utilizing thermal drone cameras.

recent_articles.title: Close contest between three-time MLA and new face with family legacy - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Bagalkot Assembly bypoll, triggered by the death of former Minister H.Y. Meti, is a tight race between **Veerabhadrayya aka Viranna Charantimath** of the BJP and first-timer Umesh Hullappa Meti of the Congress. The Congress chose Umesh, who had been handling grievances of rural voters, after internal struggles among his siblings.  The BJP hopes to capitalize on recent law and order disturbances by appealing to Hindu votes, while a Congress leader believes the incident will unite factions. Key issues include compensation for land lost to the Upper Krishna Project and expansion of irrigated areas for the third phase of the project. The constituency has seen a significant increase in voters since 1952.

recent_articles.title: Basavaraj Bommai blames Congress for delay in implementation of Upper Krishna Project - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Basavaraj Bommai**, former Chief Minister of Karnataka, criticized **Siddaramaiah** and **D.K. Shivakumar**, the current Chief Minister and Deputy Chief Minister respectively, for delaying the Upper Krishna Project (UKP) implementation.  He argued that the Congress's past inaction had hindered progress, despite receiving orders in 1975. Bommai claimed non-Congress governments were more successful in implementing the project. The matter is currently under hearing at the Supreme Court, with arguments from three states completed.

recent_articles.title: Surjewala condemns Pratap Simha’s remark against Chief Minister - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Randeep Singh Surjewala**, **AICC general secretary in-charge of Karnataka**, condemned **Pratap Simha**, a BJP leader and former MP, for his "vile remark" against **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** during the Bagalkot bypoll campaign.  Surjewala accused the BJP of using Mr. Simha to insult the Chief Minister and send a message to marginalized communities, claiming it reflects a lack of leadership within the party. He demanded an apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and state BJP leaders, as well as an FIR against Mr. Simha for his remarks.

recent_articles.title: B.P. Yatnal, expelled BJP leader, begins campaign for BJP nominee in Bagalkot - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Basanagouda Patil Yatnal**, expelled BJP leader, launched his campaign for **Veerabhadrayya Charantimath**, the BJP's candidate in the Bagalkot bypoll.  He criticized **Siddaramaiah**, the Chief Minister, and **Vijayanand Kashappanavar**, a Congress MLA, accusing them of minority appeasement policies. Yatnal also accused **Kashappanavar** of demanding IPL tickets for family members and failing to support the Panchamasali Lingayat community. He promised swift action against stone-pelting incidents if elected as Chief Minister.

recent_articles.title: Honorary doctorates to politicians raises eyebrows - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Dr. Manmohan Singh**, Bengaluru City University has awarded honorary doctorates to two politicians, **K. Govindaraj** and **B.M. Farooq**, along with other individuals including former Indian cricketer **B.K. Venkatesh Prasad** and music composer **Arjun Janya**.  The decision has sparked controversy due to concerns about the lack of uniform criteria for honorary doctorate awards and potential conflicts of interest, as highlighted by **Minister for Higher Education M.C. Sudhakar**, who had previously urged the Governor to form an expert committee on the matter.

recent_articles.title: BJP leaders practise politics of lies and double standards, says Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** of **Karnataka** criticized the **BJP**, accusing them of practicing politics based on lies and double standards. He stated that the BJP lacks integrity, credibility, and the ability to fulfill their promises.  He also accused the BJP of using divisive tactics based on caste and religion and of resorting to unfair tricks in an attempt to win the upcoming elections. **Siddaramaiah** defended his government's policies, highlighting Karnataka's economic progress under his leadership while criticizing the BJP for increasing wealth inequality across the country. He dismissed allegations of minority appeasement by the Congress as false and baseless, emphasizing equal opportunities for all communities in his government.
